title: What does select scene really score?
fullTitle: ffmpeg Scene Score: a 16-Frame Cross-Fade Scores 1/16 of a Hard Cut

scenes.narration: Select gt scene is the usual way to find cuts. What score does a hard cut get? A cross-fade? A drift? Noise? We feed ffmpeg frames we wrote ourselves, and read every score.
captions: What score does a hard cut get? A fade? Noise?
Frames we wrote ourselves, every score read.

scenes.narration: Raw frames written byte by byte in Node: one hundred sixty by ninety, sixty frames, picture A, then picture B. Cuts, fades, a drift, noise, a flash. Two readers: ffmpeg's printed score, and Node's pixel difference. Control: frame zero scores zero.
captions: 60 frames: picture A, then picture B.
Readers: ffmpeg's score, Node's pixel difference.

scenes.narration: A hard cut scores point seven seven three: the mean luma difference of the two frames, divided by a hundred. Node gets the same number from the pixels. From point one to point five, frame thirty is selected, and nothing else.

But the score is the smaller of two numbers: the difference, and how much it changed since the last frame. A flash scores point seven seven going in. Coming back, the jump is just as big, and it scores zero. Two cuts four frames apart: both caught.
captions: Score = smaller of the difference and its change.
Flash: 0.773 in, 0 out. Two cuts 4 frames apart: both caught.

scenes.narration: A cross-fade spreads the change over many frames. Its first frame scores the cut divided by the length: two frames, point three nine, four, point one nine, eight, point zero nine seven. At point one, fades of eight frames or more are never selected.
captions: First fade frame = cut score / length of the fade.
At 0.1, fades of 8 frames or more are never selected.

scenes.narration: A drift of two levels a frame scores point zero two, once. Noise: the first noisy frame scores point one nine eight, then nearly zero, though noisy frames differ more from each other than from flat. After x two six four, the cut keeps its point seven seven.
captions: Drift: 0.02 once. Noise: 0.198 on the first frame, then near 0.
After x264: the cut 0.774, the noise 0.164.

scenes.narration: Measure the scores before you pick a threshold. Cuts pass. Fades slip through, and the way back from a flash is invisible. Not tested: real footage, other encoders, other builds.
captions: Measure the scores before you pick a threshold.
Not tested: real footage, other encoders, other builds.
